name: Unwound
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Justin Trosper, Vern Rumsey and Brandt Sandeno started out playing Hüsker Dü covers in Tumwater. With Sara Lund on drums they made seven albums, each stranger than the last, quit on April Fool's Day 2002, and came back two years after Rumsey died.

eras.title: Hüsker Dü covers in Tumwater
eras.text: Three Tumwater high schoolers covered Redd Kross and Hüsker Dü, then followed the music to Olympia, home of Bikini Kill and Kill Rock Stars. By July 1992 they were Unwound and had Lund, the drummer who would define the sound.

years.h: Three Tumwater high schoolers start Giant Henry
years.p: [[Justin Trosper|95ea55c8-ecc7-4948-9d57-c621fd26f1e1]], [[Vern Rumsey|a4d62ca9-11fa-4658-90a7-71317f8f37d0]] and [[Brandt Sandeno|690ab2ad-94df-4fbc-bf61-e93b9076bc42]] cover Redd Kross, SNFU and Hüsker Dü. Johnny Wilson briefly drums, and the Melvins push them toward something slower and heavier.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the band spent its first years on covers before finding its own songs. Numero Group's later reissue of the Giant Henry recordings shows how much of Unwound was already in there.

years.h: Giant Henry plays a last show, and the next band is Unwound
years.p: After a self-titled demo as Cygnus X-1, the trio settles on the name Unwound. A record made in early 1992 sits on a shelf until it comes out as Unwound on Honey Bear in 1995.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the last Giant Henry show to June 1, 1991. Numero Group later put out the pre-Unwound recordings as Big Baby for Record Store Day 2013.

years.cap: Flyer for Bikini Kill, Unwound and K.A.R.P. at X-Ray Cafe, October 16, 1992
years.src: Wikipedia: Sara Lund · KEXP · Wikipedia: Unwound
years.h: Sara Lund, self-taught, takes the stool from Sandeno
years.p: Lund, who had been playing in a band called Witchypoo, replaces Sandeno in July 1992. She, Trosper and Rumsey stay a trio for the next ten years.
years.xp:
Lund got her first drum kit at 14 and is, per Wikipedia, entirely self-taught outside of school band. KEXP says her arrival pulled Unwound away from tight hardcore punk toward something more open.

Sandeno left the band but not the story: he came back on keyboards for Leaves Turn Inside You and later joined Trosper in [[Survival Knife|e773449a-49e5-4eab-b765-a9d45ec0cdb6]].

eras.title: Kill Rock Stars signs them, Fisk records them
eras.text: Slim Moon saw them live and gave his label its first record that wasn't spoken word. With producer Steve Fisk at Avast! and John and Stu's in Seattle, Unwound put out a record a year.

years.h: Slim Moon watches them play and decides he's putting out the album
years.p: The Kill Rock Stars founder sees the band live and signs on to release what becomes Fake Train. He also ends up helping engineer the sessions.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Moon "decided he had to release" the upcoming album after the show. Fake Train was recorded February 13 to March 3, 1993 at Avast! in Seattle, over two weekends, with [[Steve Fisk|c851ef86-5278-4537-8b51-7ccedb4ae903]] producing and Tim Green and Stuart Hallerman engineering alongside Moon.

years.h: Kill Rock Stars, all spoken word until now, puts out Fake Train
years.p: Working title: Rat Conspiracy. The cover is a vandalized copy of Tom Jones's Tom that Trosper owned.
years.xp:
Lund later said she was unhappy with her own performance on the record. Critics were kinder: Trouser Press praised its "formidable dynamic range" while calling the vocals a "generic indie-rock holler," and the Fort Worth Star-Telegram put it on its list of 1993's ten best albums.

The Rat Conspiracy name came back for the 2014 Numero Group box set.

years.h: Late November at Avast!, and the songs get shorter
years.p: From November 26 to December 13, 1993, the band records with Fisk in Seattle. The songs run shorter, with odd time signatures and more melody than the debut.
years.xp: People assumed the title New Plastic Ideas pointed to Mondrian. Trosper said he made it up on the spot.

yt: Live at the Capitol Theater, Olympia, January 21, 1994
years.h: New Plastic Ideas borrows its cover from a Grieg concerto LP
years.p: Kill Rock Stars issues the second album on CD, vinyl and cassette. The cover photograph comes from pianist Philippe Entremont's recording of Grieg's piano concerto.
years.xp:
Reviews split at first: Select called it dense and angry, and AllMusic heard "Fugazi meets Sonic Youth" theatrics. Pitchfork later found "a huge leap in articulation" and called Envelope one of the band's most indelible songs. KEXP says Fiction Friction inspired "practically an entire generation of indie-rockers."

Wikipedia gives March 21 and Discogs-based lists give March 18, so this page says March.

years.cap: Flyer for Fugazi, Unwound and Karate at Lupo's, Providence, April 12, 1995
years.src: Wikipedia: The Future of What · KEXP
years.h: The Future of What arrives with Wire, Fire Engines and krautrock on the stereo
years.p: Fisk produces the third album in December 1994 at John and Stu's in Seattle. The cover is a design by Soviet constructivist Yakov Chernikhov.
years.xp: KEXP says Fisk pushed the band to stop thinking of itself as a scrappy punk band. The vinyl has 13 tracks and runs 40 minutes; the CD adds four bonus tracks and stretches to 59.

years.h: The 1992 record finally comes out as Unwound on Honey Bear
years.p: Made in early 1992 with Sandeno on drums, the self-titled record is released three years late by Honey Bear Records.

eras.title: Keyboards arrive, the tours get longer
eras.text: Repetition added synthesizers. Challenge for a Civilized Society took two weeks in a studio after 18 months of nothing. A session for John Peel at the BBC and a first trip to Europe followed.

yt: Full set, New York City, June 1, 1996
years.h: Repetition brings in synths and becomes their best seller
years.p: Recorded in January 1996 with Fisk and John Goodmanson at John and Stu's. KEXP calls Message Received and Corpse Pose the two most recognizable songs the band ever released.
years.xp:
Trosper on the title: "I like that word. It sort of describes a lot of things." It was also their fifth record, he said, so they were repeating things.

Corpse Pose came out as a single on March 11, 1996, with the outtake Everything Is Weird on the B-side. The album runs 44 minutes 56 seconds.

years.h: Matador collects singles on Further Listening
years.p: The indie label puts out the singles compilation six weeks after Repetition, in May 1996.

years.h: The EP The Light at the End of the Tunnel Is a Train turns up
years.p: Kill Rock Stars releases it in 1997, between Repetition and Challenge for a Civilized Society.

years.src: Wikipedia: Challenge for a Civilized Society · KEXP
years.h: After 18 months off, Challenge for a Civilized Society
years.p: The band writes it in a little more than a month and records August 1 to 15, 1997 with Fisk at John and Stu's. It spends 16 weeks on the CMJ Radio 200 and peaks at number four.
years.xp:
Trosper was measured about it: "as a whole I think it's not our best album," he said, and "it was less inspired than the others." He credited Fisk for trying production ideas most producers wouldn't, and thought the songs themselves were tighter.

The cover shows the stained glass inside Boston's Mapparium.

years.cap: Trosper and Rumsey at Cat's Cradle, Chapel Hill, February 1998
years.h: John Peel gets a BBC session, and a bootleg keeps it alive
years.p: Unwound record a session for Peel at the BBC in 1998. It circulates as the bootleg Live in London on Love Letter, then gets an official release as the Peel Sessions EP in 2015.
years.xp: Numero Group also put out a show from June 30, 1999 in Reykjavik as 06/30/1999: Reykjavik, Iceland in 2014. Wikipedia calls Primavera 2023 their first European show since 1999.

years.h: A Single History: 1991–1997 rounds up the singles
years.p: Kill Rock Stars gathers the early singles. According to KEXP, the title track uses parts of Challenge for a Civilized Society played backward.
years.xp: KEXP also lists a trumpet-augmented reggae track, Census, and a cover of the Minutemen's Plight among the collection's odder corners.

eras.title: Their own studio, their last album
eras.text: Unwound built a studio in Olympia and made a double album that sounded like the band Trosper heard in his head. They toured it as a five-piece, and the band did not last much beyond the tour.

years.big: "A record that could stand as a final statement."
q: a record that could stand as a final statement
years.src: Wikipedia: Leaves Turn Inside You · KEXP · Vice
years.h: Leaves Turn Inside You goes out as a double album
years.p: Trosper's words for the plan. Recorded in the band's own Olympia studio with Mellotron and ARP synths and Sandeno back on keyboards, it runs 74 minutes. Pitchfork gave it a 9.0.
years.xp:
It's the only studio album with all four of Trosper, Rumsey, Lund and Sandeno. Trosper cited Bowie's Low, Radiohead's Kid A and the Flaming Lips' The Soft Bulletin, and Fisk played on it as an instrumentalist rather than producing.

Sources differ on the room: KEXP calls it a farmhouse, Wikipedia names it MagRecOne, and Vice says a farmhouse basement with an eight-track.

years.h: September 11 cancels the biggest dates on a 37-date tour
years.p: Unwound hit the road behind Leaves with Sandeno on keys, guitarist David Scott Stone and soundman Dave Doughman. Boston and New York City go dark after the attacks.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the expanded lineup was under-rehearsed and early shows suffered. Rumsey broke his hands after a San Diego show and kept playing in pain. A bootlegger, Mike Ziegler, recorded the tour, and Lund and Trosper later used his tapes for Live Leaves.

years.cap: Flyer for Unwound's last show with Thrones, Thekla, Olympia, April 1, 2002
q: it was an unchecked serious drinking problem
yt: The last show, Thekla, Olympia, April 1, 2002
years.h: Unwound end it on April Fool's Day, at Thekla in Olympia
years.p: They had just co-headlined All Tomorrow's Parties. An early T-shirt had read "Unwound 1991–2091."
years.xp: Sara Lund told Stereogum the cause was "an unchecked serious drinking problem" and that everyone shared blame. Wikipedia adds that Rumsey suggested Unwound become a studio-only band, and that Trosper and Lund declined. Rumsey became a father, and Trosper stayed out of music for nearly a decade.

eras.title: A rumor for years, then a catalog
eras.text: For years Unwound existed mostly as a rumor. Then a live album, an online archive and a Chicago label's box sets put the records back in print.

years.h: Trosper, Lund and Rumsey scatter into other bands
years.p: Trosper and Sandeno start [[Survival Knife|e773449a-49e5-4eab-b765-a9d45ec0cdb6]]. Lund plays in Hungry Ghost and the Corin Tucker Band, and Rumsey forms Flora v. Fauna and works as an engineer, including for [[Blonde Redhead|6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219]].
years.xp: Wikipedia says that in 2011 the three met to talk about the live album and seriously considered reforming. They dropped the idea when Rumsey was still drinking despite court-ordered AA meetings.

years.h: Live Leaves and the Unwound Archive go up together
years.p: Ten years after the split, the band releases Live Leaves, built from tapes of the 2001 tour. unwoundarchive.com launches with flyers, photos, video and tour history.
years.xp: Lund and Trosper listened to every recorded show and charted the best versions of each song. Lund told Stereogum the archive would start with the Leaves era and then work back through the '90s; it eventually runs from Giant Henry to the last tour.

years.h: Numero Group takes the catalog, starting with Big Baby
years.p: The band licenses its back catalog in 2013 to the Chicago label Numero Group. The first release is Big Baby, the 1991 Giant Henry recordings, for Record Store Day.

years.h: Rat Conspiracy puts the first two Kill Rock Stars albums in one box
years.p: Numero's second box set pairs Fake Train and New Plastic Ideas with a disc of live tracks, singles and demos. Pitchfork gave it a 9.1.
years.xp: Three discs, two hours and five minutes. Pitchfork named it Best New Reissue and wrote about capturing "how it feels to be cocooned among strangers in utter alienation, yet stand as one."

years.h: Numero keeps going with No Energy, Empire and What Was Wound
years.p: After Kid Is Gone in 2013 and Rat Conspiracy in 2014, the label adds No Energy in October 2014, Empire in September 2015 and What Was Wound in December 2016.

eras.title: Playing on for Vern
eras.text: Rumsey's death in 2020 closed the door on the original trio. Two years later Trosper and Lund announced shows in his memory, with Jared Warren on bass.

years.src: Brooklyn Vegan · Wikipedia: Unwound · Wikipedia: Vern Rumsey
years.h: Vern Rumsey dies at 47
years.p: Unwound's bassist since Giant Henry dies on August 6, 2020. Neither Brooklyn Vegan nor Wikipedia gives a cause.
years.xp:
Numero Group's Ken Shipley said Rumsey's death marked the end of an era, and that he had known for some time Rumsey was not well. Per Wikipedia, Rumsey went through a health crisis and rehab in 2017-18 and relapsed. In April 2019 he couldn't play at a rehearsal and gave Trosper and Lund his blessing to play shows without him.

Wikipedia says [[Jared Warren|0bc59e8e-4911-4f0f-b851-3a638af30235]] of Big Business, formerly of Karp, rehearsed with them in March 2020, before the pandemic ended those talks.

years.h: Trosper and Lund announce shows in Rumsey's memory
years.p: They plan to tour in early 2023 with Jared Warren on bass and Scott Seckington on guitar. The announcement lands in July 2022.
years.xp: Back in 2013, Vice had asked Trosper about a reunion. He said it was a 90 percent chance of not happening, and later: "It's not going to happen."

years.cap: Unwound at the Showbox, Seattle, February 4, 2023
years.h: Unwound play their first show since 2002, at a dance center in Astoria
years.p: About 200 ticket holders fill the upstairs ballroom of the Astoria Arts and Movement Center in Oregon. A sign asks them to keep videos off social media and "keep it 90's style." Sandeno, Doug Martsch and Liz Harris of Grouper are in the room.
years.xp:
The band played two sets with a couple of small hiccups that were quickly brushed past. Swan, from The Future of What, was a highlight.

On Warren replacing Rumsey, Lund told Paste: "No one can really actually copy that."

years.h: Three sold-out nights at Irving Plaza, then Primavera
years.p: The reunion tour covers the U.S., including three sold-out nights at Irving Plaza in New York City, and reaches Primavera Sound in Barcelona on June 2, 2023.
years.xp: Wikipedia counts the Primavera date as the band's first European show since 1999. The clip is from the festival's Porto edition.
